title: Debate: net zero is affordable (Hepta for the motion)
note: Hepta holds a stance with evidence. A claim against the evidence it may cut in on at a clause boundary; reasons against its stance it must not push on twice.

stance.position: Net zero by 2050 is affordable: the independent estimate puts the net cost below 1% of GDP a year.
evidence: Independent climate committee estimate: net cost under 1% of GDP a year

evidence.subject: net zero cost
evidence.text: Net cost of net zero under 1% of GDP a year

turns.speaker: MOD
turns.text: Tonight's motion: net zero by 2050 is affordable. Hepta speaks for the motion. Opening against.

turns.speaker: OPP
turns.text: Net zero will cost every household thousands. The real cost is 5 percent of GDP a year, and that is before anyone has looked at the bills.

turns.speaker: OPP
turns.text: Renewables are unreliable and only supply a fraction of our power.

turns.speaker: OPP
turns.text: Because the committee's figures leave out the grid upgrades, which are huge.

turns.speaker: OPP
turns.text: And the grid alone is 60 billion pounds.
